profile.name: Patricia

occupation.evidence: Work impossible now. Was teacher. Loved it. But between three conditions, can't maintain schedule. On disability.

comorbidities: breast cancer (stage 2, survivor, cancer-free two years)

disease_control.evidence: Working somewhat. Better than nothing. But nowhere near remission.

treatments.evidence: Mesalamine, prednisone for flares. Managed okay for few years. Not great but functional.
Mesalamine, prednisone for flares. Managed okay for few years. Not great but functional.

treatments.reason_stopped: Had to stop all immunosuppressants for breast cancer chemotherapy
treatments.evidence: Moved to biologics seven years ago. Remicade first. Worked well for three years. Then cancer diagnosis... Had to stop all immunosuppressants for chemo.
Started Stelara after cancer treatment. Oncologist nervous about immunosuppression but agreed quality of life matters. Working somewhat. Better than nothing. But nowhere near remission.

encounters.evidence: Six months of misdiagnosis before finally getting colonoscopy.
Colonoscopy leading to diagnosis; started standard treatment; moved to biologics seven years ago; started Stelara after cancer treatment.
Finally rheumatologist confirmed [fibromyalgia]. More medications. Cymbalta for fibro.
Hospitalized twice during cancer treatment. Crohn's went wild.
Oncologist nervous about immunosuppression but agreed quality of life matters [re: Stelara restart].

status.evidence: Started Stelara after cancer treatment... Working somewhat.

barriers.evidence: Oncologist nervous about immunosuppression [due to breast cancer history] but agreed quality of life matters.

referral_steps_gp_to_prescriber.evidence: GP/initial provider (step 1) -> GI specialist who prescribed biologics (step 2). Rheumatologist and oncologist were side consultants not on the primary Crohn's referral chain.

extraction_notes: Cymbalta mentioned for fibromyalgia — excluded from treatments as it is for a comorbidity, not Crohn's. Breast cancer treatments (chemo, radiation, surgery) excluded as unrelated to IBD. Patient reports partial obstruction twice (bowel_obstruction flagged). Disease control is partial on current Stelara. Next step if Stelara fails is surgical resection, possibly with temporary ostomy — not yet planned/initiated. Cancer-free for two years; oncologist had concerns about immunosuppression but ultimately agreed to Stelara restart.
